transcript.content:
hey, i'm berry

tell me your dream, however it comes back to you. bits and pieces are fine

hey berry. ok so the part that stuck with me most is my grandfather. he died years ago but in the dream we were sitting across from each other on this old train at night, going through snow. he had a brown leather suitcase on his knees

it was really quiet

your grandfather, a suitcase on his knees, snow going by in the dark. and all that quiet

did either of you say anything?

no, he didn't say a word. i don't remember if i said anything either. he just opened the suitcase and held it out so i could see inside

it was full of letters. like hundreds of them, all addressed to me

hundreds of letters, all with your name on them

did you open any of them?

don't think so, i don't remember opening any. i just looked at them

then the train stopped, right in the middle of a snowy field. nowhere near a station or anything

just stopped, out in the middle of all that snow

what happened once it stopped?

we got off together and walked through the snow, it was deep. there was this red door just standing on its own out there. no house or anything around it, just the door in its frame

that's where we were heading

a red door just standing out there in the snow, no house, nothing

when you were walking toward it with him, were you yourself, like you seeing through your own eyes? or more like watching the two of you from somewhere else?

honestly i don't remember, i never really thought about that. it was just happening

when we got to the door he gave me the suitcase and nodded at it, like go on. so i opened it and there was this warm yellow light on the other side

that's where it ended

that's okay, dreams don't really give you that part

him handing you the suitcase and nodding, then the door opening onto warm yellow light

that red door out there on its own, what was it like up close?

honestly i don't remember much about it up close. just that it was red and standing there in its frame on its own. i don't remember what it was made of or anything like that

the light when it opened is what i remember more

that's fine, the light's the part that stayed

was it different from how things felt back on the train?

yeah i guess so. on the train everything outside was white and blue, cold looking, and so quiet. then the door opened and it was warm yellow light, so it was kind of the opposite of all that

i don't really remember how i felt though, just how it looked

cold blue and white the whole way, then that warm yellow when the door opened

and he'd had that brown leather suitcase on his knees the whole ride. did it feel like it mattered, or was it just something he was carrying?

i think it mattered? i mean it was full of letters to me, and he made a point of showing me. and then at the door he handed it over to me like it was mine now

but i don't really remember feeling anything about it in the dream. that's more me thinking about it now

handed it over like it was yours now. that's fair, the thinking about it can come after

the train at night going through snow, is that the first thing you remember? or was there something before you were sitting across from him?
yeah the train's the first thing i remember. i was just already sitting there across from him, no idea how i got on or anything before that

already sitting there, no way on. that's how they go

okay so here's how i've got it. you're on an old train at night, going through snow, sitting across from your grandfather, who died years ago. it's really quiet. he's got a brown leather suitcase on his knees, and without saying a word he opens it and holds it out so you can see. it's full of letters, hundreds of them, all addressed to you. you just look at them

then the train stops right in the middle of a snowy field, nowhere near a station. you get off together and walk through deep snow toward a red door standing on its own in its frame, no house around it. outside it's all white and blue and cold looking the whole way. at the door he gives you the suitcase and nods, like go on. you open it and there's warm yellow light on the other side, and that's where it ends

did i get that right, or did i miss anything?

yeah that's pretty much it. one small thing, the white and blue is what i remember seeing out the train window. i don't really remember what the colors were like once we were walking, just that it was deep snow. otherwise that's right

got it, the white and blue was out the train window. once you were off and walking it's just deep snow

so it's you and him walking through deep snow to that red door, him handing you the suitcase, and the warm yellow light when you open it. is that how it went now?
yeah that's how it went. he nodded at the door when he gave me the suitcase, then i opened it and there was the light

him nodding at the door, then the light. okay, i've got it

would you like to see it drawn?
yeah, i'd like that

okay. there are a few ways it could look. soft watercolour, quiet and tender, like a memory that's been gently kept. or an old woodcut print, plain and solemn, like a story told once and never forgotten. or a deep blue cyanotype, hushed and faraway, like an old photo of something that never quite happened. or a quiet night photo, just how it looked to you, cold blue and white out the train window, then that warm yellow

which feels closest? or you can tell me your own way
the last one i think, the night photo. that's closest to how it looked, the cold blue out the window and then the yellow light

night photo it is. i'll start with your grandfather

i'm picturing him as an old man with a lined face and white hair, in a heavy winter coat over plain old-fashioned clothes. those are just my guesses, you didn't say

anything different about him, or would you leave that to me?
i don't really remember what he looked like in the dream or what he was wearing, so go with your guess. that sounds fine to me

okay, i'm sketching your grandfather, the snowy field and the suitcase now. it'll show up on the right

for the old train, i'm seeing it at night, with that cold white and blue outside. my guesses are the rest: facing seats, and the window with snow and darkness going by

anything different about the train, or would you leave it to me?

that sounds right. we were sitting across from each other so facing seats fits. out the window i mostly remember it being white and blue though, more than dark. and it was really quiet, just the two of us that i remember. the rest go with your guess

okay, i'm sketching the old train now, white and blue out the window, just the two of you. it'll show up on the right

would you like to be drawn as you are, and tell me a little about yourself? or should i just imagine you?
just imagine me, that's fine. i don't really remember what i looked like in the dream anyway, i was just kind of there

that's fine, i'll imagine you. i'm sketching you now

everything's being sketched and it'll show up on the right over the next minute or two. if anything looks wrong once it's there, just tell me
ok they're all there. yeah they look right to me, that's pretty much how i remember it. thanks berry

thank you for telling me all of it

him holding that suitcase of letters out to you on the quiet train, then handing it over at the red door and nodding you through into that warm yellow light. i'm really glad i got to see it with you
